alex: quick heads-up — our async python sample app started failing with quota/rl checks. got a 429 + headers that look inconsistent across replicas, e.g. remaining going negative. cc @morgan

morgan: ugh, yeah i've seen variants of this. sometimes the gateway returns both X-RateLimit-* and X-Quota-* and they don't line up. our merge logic in the async client might be overwriting instead of taking the safe min.

priya: can you paste the raw headers + the 429 response you saw?

alex: pasted below (redacted keys):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: -5
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000000
X-Quota-Remaining: 10
X-Quota-Window: 60
Retry-After: 120
Retry-After-MS: 120000
Content-Type: application/json
```

alex: reproduced locally by hitting with concurrency=40. client then tried to merge server-side quotas into a shared token-bucket and ended up allowing extra bursts later (race + negative clamp bug).

morgan: two quick notes: 1) Negative "Remaining" should be clamped to 0 immediately (we can't trust callers to handle negatives). 2) In async flows we must update the per-key quota atomically — current implementation does read-modify-write without a lock which loses to concurrent responses.

priya: agree. also we need a clear heuristic for Retry-After vs Retry-After-MS: prefer Retry-After-MS when present (treat as ms), else parse Retry-After as seconds. but also detect mis-set units: if Retry-After > 3600 treat as likely ms and convert if there's no Retry-After-MS header. document this behavior so integrators know why we chose it.

matt: sounds good. for the SDK API surface i propose adding two helpers: parse_rate_limit_headers(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> Mapping[str, int] and parse_retry_after(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> float (seconds). typed signatures (typing.Mapping, float) are fine for sync and async code. we should also add an async-safe TokenBucket.update_from_headers(headers) coroutine that takes an asyncio.Lock or uses an internal lock.

alex: i've sketched a minimal typed helper in the sample app to validate assumptions:
```py
from typing import Mapping, Tuple

def parse_retry_after(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> float:
    # prefer ms header if present
    if 'retry-after-ms' in headers:
        return int(headers['retry-after-ms']) / 1000.0
    if 'retry-after' in headers:
        v = float(headers['retry-after'])
        if v > 3600:  # heuristic: likely ms mis-sent
            return v / 1000.0
        return v
    return 0.0

# return (limit, remaining, reset_ts) as ints, clamp remaining >= 0
def parse_rl_headers(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
    limit = int(headers.get('x-ratelimit-limit', '0'))
    remaining = max(0, int(headers.get('x-ratelimit-remaining', '0')))
    reset = int(headers.get('x-ratelimit-reset', '0'))
    return (limit, remaining, reset)
```

priya: nice. couple of followups: - canonicalize header keys to lower-case early (headers are often mixed-case). - unit tests for both ms/seconds cases + malformed values. - add a small integration test that runs with 20 concurrent requests to ensure atomic update prevents double-crediting.

morgan: for typing return values i'd prefer a simple NamedTuple or TypedDict so callers can destructure sensibly in both sync/async code. e.g. RateInfo = TypedDict('RateInfo', {'limit': int, 'remaining': int, 'reset': int}). keeps mypy happy.

matt: can someone open an issue and PR? i'll shepherd and add release note entry. include test vectors and the concurrency integration test.

alex: created draft PR at https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py-sdk/pull/2345 — includes parse_retry_after, parse_rl_headers, clamp logic, and an async TokenBucket.update_from_headers that uses an internal asyncio.Lock. also added unit tests for Retry-After ms/sec heuristics. still needs typing cleanup per morgan + a doc blurb.

ci-bot: PR 2345 opened by alex — tests pending :github: CI

morgan: i'll review today. if we land the helper we'll call it from the high-level client so both sync/async paths share the exact merge semantics. also add a debug flag to log raw headers when --dev to help troubleshoot.

alex: thanks — i'll iterate on the typing and add a short sample-app README reproducer. :thumbsup:
